method_card.title: Mode, Median and Mean for Ungrouped Data
method_card.content:
There are three averages you need to calculate from a raw (ungrouped) list of values. Each measures the centre of the data differently, and choosing the right one depends on the shape of the data and the context.

The mode is the value that appears most often. It is the only average that works with non-numerical (categorical) data, but it can be misleading if two very different values share equal frequency. The mode is not affected by extreme values.

The median is the middle value once the data are ordered from smallest to largest. For \(n\) values where \(n\) is odd, the median is the \(\frac{n+1}{2}\)th value. For even \(n\), it is the mean of the two middle values. The median is resistant to outliers, making it ideal for skewed distributions such as house prices or salaries.

The arithmetic mean is \(\bar{x} = \frac{\sum x}{n}\). It uses every data point and is the most mathematically complete average — but it is pulled towards outliers. If one extreme value is present, the mean can misrepresent the typical value.

Choosing the right average: use the mode for categorical data; use the median when data are skewed or outliers are present; use the mean when data are roughly symmetrical and you want to include all values.
steps: Order the data from smallest to largest before finding the median
Identify the mode by counting how often each value appears
Find the median position using \(\frac{n+1}{2}\) for odd \(n\), or average the two middle values for even \(n\)
State which average is most appropriate and explain why in context

exam_context.marks: 2–4 marks (calculation); up to 3 marks for justifying appropriate average in context
exam_context.frequency: Appears on every paper; justification questions are high-frequency in the interpretation sections

worked_examples.question: Ages of 7 students: 14, 16, 15, 14, 17, 14, 18. Calculate mean and mode. Which is more appropriate?

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: The mean (15.4) is more appropriate: no extreme outliers, and it uses all seven values. The mode (14) understates the typical age.

worked_examples.question: House prices (thousands): 120, 135, 142, 150, 155, 160, 168, 950. Calculate mean and median. Which better represents the typical price?

steps.label: Step 2 — Median
steps.content: \(n = 8\). Median = mean of 4th and 5th values: \((150+155) \div 2 = 152.5\) thousand.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: The median (152.5) is better. The value 950 is an outlier that pulls the mean up to 247.5, higher than 7 of the 8 houses. The median is not affected by this extreme value.

misconceptions.message: 7 appears three times; 4 appears twice. The mode is 7.
Order first: 3, 7, 9, 11, 15. The median is the 3rd value = 9.

bronze.display: A dataset has 7 values. At which position is the median?
Find the median of the ordered list: 2, 5, 8, 11.

misconceptions.message: Even n=4. Median = mean of 2nd and 3rd values: (5+8)/2 = 6.5.

bronze.display: Which average is most appropriate for categorical data such as favourite subject?

misconceptions.message: Only the mode works with non-numerical categorical data.

bronze.display: A dataset is: 6, 6, 7, 8, 9. What is the mode?

misconceptions.message: 6 appears twice; all others appear once. Mode = 6.
Sum = 15. Mean = 15 ÷ 5 = 3. When all values are equal, the mean equals that value.

silver.display: Scores of 9 students: 45, 62, 38, 62, 71, 55, 62, 48, 90. Find the median.
Temperatures over 6 days: 12, 15, 18, 9, 22, 14. Calculate the mean.
A dataset contains one very large outlier. Which average is least affected?

misconceptions.message: The median is the middle value and is not pulled towards extreme values.

silver.display: Five friends earn per week: £220, £240, £250, £260, £1500. Mean = £494, median = £250. Which better represents typical earnings?
options: Mean (£494), because it uses all five values
Median (£250), because £1500 is an outlier distorting the mean

misconceptions.message: £1500 is an outlier. The median (£250) better represents the typical wage.

silver.display: A dataset of 11 values has sum 374. What is the mean?
A dataset has mean 20 and 5 values. One value is removed; new mean of 4 values is 18. What was the removed value?

misconceptions.message: Original sum = 100. New sum = 72. Removed value = 100 − 72 = 28.

gold.display: Ten values have mean 8. A new value of 18 is added. What is the new mean to 1 decimal place?
A dataset of 7 values has median 14. An 8th value of 25 is added. With n=8, the new median is the mean of which two positions?

misconceptions.message: With n=8, median = mean of 4th and 5th values.

gold.display: Step counts over 9 days: 4200, 6800, 7100, 5500, 9900, 6800, 7200, 6800, 32000. Which average best represents typical daily steps?
options: Median (6800), because the 32000 outlier distorts the mean
Mean (about 9589), because it uses all nine data points
Mode (6800), as it is the same as the median

misconceptions.message: 32000 is an extreme outlier. Median = 5th value = 6800. Mean ≈ 9589. The median is more representative.

gold.display: A dataset has 5 values. Four are 3, 7, 9, 11. The mean of all 5 is 8. What is the fifth value?

misconceptions.message: Required sum = 40. Known sum = 30. Missing value = 10.

gold.display: A positively skewed distribution has mean 45, median 38, mode 30. What does positive skew mean here?
options: Most values are high; a few low values drag the mean down
Most values are low; a few high values pull the mean upward
Mean, median and mode are equal

misconceptions.message: Positive skew: tail extends to the right. Mean (45) > median (38) > mode (30) confirms positive skew.
